questions.q: Why does the validation gate compare the candidate with the production model instead of only checking a minimum AUC?
options: Because a minimum AUC cannot be computed
Because a candidate can clear an absolute floor and still be clearly worse than the model it replaces
Because production models never change
Because comparisons are faster than thresholds
questions.explain: In the lesson, candidate B scored 0.752, just above the 0.75 floor, but was 0.05 AUC below production; only the comparison caught it.

questions.q: Why must both models be evaluated on the same fixed holdout that neither trained on?
options: So the difference reflects the models, not different data or leakage
So the holdout can be used to train the next model
Because holdouts must be exactly 800 rows
So that calibration is always perfect
questions.explain: A fair comparison uses identical unseen rows for both models. Different data or training rows would confound the result.

questions.q: How does the validation script make a CI step fail when the candidate is rejected?
options: It deletes the candidate model file
It prints the word FAIL in red
It emails the team automatically
It exits with a non-zero exit code
questions.explain: CI systems treat a non-zero exit code from a command as a failed step, which stops the job.

questions.q: Candidate C scored AUC 0.798 against production's 0.802 and was approved. Why?
options: The gate is broken
The 0.004 drop is inside the 0.01 tolerance, which is a policy choice
Candidates with regularization are always approved
Because slice checks are skipped for regularized models
questions.explain: MAX_DROP = 0.01 lets small differences pass. Given the noise on an 800-row holdout, where the interval is about 0.767 to 0.834, that is a reasonable but documented choice.

questions.q: What does the lesson's bootstrap of the 800-row holdout show?
options: The AUC is exactly 0.802 with no uncertainty
The holdout should be smaller
The AUC has a wide 95% interval (about 0.767 to 0.834), so tiny differences between models are within noise
Bootstrapping fixes calibration
questions.explain: Resampling shows how much AUC varies with a small holdout, which is why tolerances are policy and larger holdouts help.
